verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes concrete rendering acceptance conditions: chapter images must preserve their proportions and must not be unintentionally cropped.
First concrete failure: several chapter images appeared elongated and the Chapter 15 image was visibly cropped.
Adds an implementation-relevant acceptance condition requiring full-page chapter images to be checked for pixelation; no prior attribute becomes obsolete.
Distinct failure evidence: the rendered images exhibit a new four-corner artifact, while different chapter images are also partially cropped.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Nadia, I have a few points:
1\. The content updates I made in the last file I sent were missing from manuscript\_final7.docx. I have therefore made those edits again and am sharing another updated document here; please use this version.
2\. In the video you shared, most images appear to have strange curved lines at 4 corners. Please review them.
3\. Could the text under Mama's Hot Take be formatted in italics?
4\. I am sharing the pictures again for replacement because the images for the Social Media chapter and What to Say Instead are partially cut and need updating.
5\. From the video, some pages looked visually heavy because they contained a lot of text. Could we add more spacing, at least between paragraphs, so those pages feel lighter?

value_updates.corner_artifact_prevention: Chapter images must render without strange curved lines at their corners.
